definitions.explanation: Sushi made by rolling vinegared rice and fillings in a sheet of seaweed (nori), then cutting it into rounds. A staple of Japanese home cooking and sushi restaurants.

examples.japanese: {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}る。
{節分|せつぶん}には{恵方|えほう}{巻|ま}きという{巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: On Setsubun, people eat a sushi roll called ehomaki.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}がお{弁当|べんとう}に{入|い}れてくれた{巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}は、{卵焼|たまごや}きとキュウリが{入|はい}っていて{美味|おい}しかった。
examples.english: The sushi rolls my mother put in my lunch box had egg omelet and cucumber in them and were delicious.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
{巻|ま}き (rolling) + {寿司|ずし} (sushi). Also written {巻|ま}きずし or {巻寿司|まきずし}.

USAGE:
{巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし} has several varieties based on thickness:
- {太巻|ふとま}き: thick roll with multiple fillings
- {細巻|ほそま}き: thin roll with a single filling (e.g., かっぱ{巻|ま}き for cucumber, {鉄火|てっか}{巻|ま}き for tuna)
- {裏巻|うらま}き: inside-out roll (rice on outside)

Rolling is done with a {巻|ま}きす (bamboo rolling mat). {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし} is commonly made at home for celebrations, parties, and {弁当|べんとう} (lunch boxes).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}を{巻|ま}く: to roll sushi
- {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}を{切|き}る: to cut sushi rolls
- {手作|てづく}り{巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}: homemade sushi rolls
